\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{هاجر} (hājara)}{هاجر (hājara)}]{\ar{هاجر} (hājara) — to emigrate}

\label{lesson:AR-C332-hajara-emigrate}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to flourish, then the Arabic for an emperor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{هاجر}}
\textbf{\ar{هاجر}} — \emph{hājara} — \textquotedblleft{}to emigrate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{هاجر} \ar{عمي} \ar{إلى} \ar{بلد} \ar{بعيد} \ar{قبل} \ar{عشرين} \ar{سنة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hājara ʿammī ilā balad baʿīd qabla ʿishrīn sana.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle emigrated to a distant country twenty years ago.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يهاجر}, \emph{yuhājir}.

An emigrant is \ar{مهاجر}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{هاجر}} (\emph{hājara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{h-j-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to leave, to cut oneself off from\textquotedblright{}. It is Form III, \textquotedblleft{}to leave one's land for another\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hājara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hājara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hājara ʿammī ilā balad baʿīd qabla ʿishrīn sana.} — My uncle emigrated to a distant country twenty years ago.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to flourish, then the Arabic for an emperor, then say \emph{hājara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{هاجر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To emigrate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استقر} (istaqarra)}{استقر (istaqarra)}]{\ar{استقر} (istaqarra) — to settle down}

\label{lesson:AR-C332-istaqarra}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an emperor, then the Arabic for to emigrate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استقر}}
\textbf{\ar{استقر}} — \emph{istaqarra} — \textquotedblleft{}to settle down\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استقرت} \ar{الأسرة} \ar{في} \ar{مدينة} \ar{على} \ar{البحر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istaqarrat al-usra fī madīna ʿalā al-baḥr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The family settled in a city by the sea.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستقر}, \emph{yastaqirr}.

Of a situation: \ar{استقر} \ar{الوضع}, things calmed down.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استقر}} (\emph{istaqarra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-r-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to stay in a place, to be at rest\textquotedblright{}. It is Form X, \textquotedblleft{}to come to rest\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaqarra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaqarra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaqarrat al-usra fī madīna ʿalā al-baḥr.} — The family settled in a city by the sea.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an emperor, then the Arabic for to emigrate, then say \emph{istaqarra} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{استقر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To settle down\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رحل} (raḥala)}{رحل (raḥala)}]{\ar{رحل} (raḥala) — to move out; to depart}

\label{lesson:AR-C332-rahala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to emigrate, then the Arabic for to settle down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رحل}}
\textbf{\ar{رحل}} — \emph{raḥala} — \textquotedblleft{}to move out; to depart\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رحل} \ar{الجيران} \ar{عن} \ar{الحي} \ar{الشهر} \ar{الماضي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{raḥala al-jīrān ʿan al-ḥayy ash-shahr al-māḍī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The neighbours moved out of the area last month.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرحل}, \emph{yarḥal}.

Of a person who died: \ar{رحل} \ar{عنا}, he has left us.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رحل}} (\emph{raḥala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-ḥ-l} (Lane), where \emph{raḥl} is a camel saddle and \emph{raḥala}, \textquotedblleft{}to set off\textquotedblright{}; the taught \emph{riḥla}, a journey, shares it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raḥala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raḥala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raḥala al-jīrān ʿan al-ḥayy ash-shahr al-māḍī.} — The neighbours moved out of the area last month.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to emigrate, then the Arabic for to settle down, then say \emph{raḥala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{رحل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To move out; to depart\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نزح} (nazaḥa)}{نزح (nazaḥa)}]{\ar{نزح} (nazaḥa) — to be displaced, to flee one’s home}

\label{lesson:AR-C332-nazaha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to settle down, then the Arabic for to move out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نزح}}
\textbf{\ar{نزح}} — \emph{nazaḥa} — \textquotedblleft{}to be displaced, to flee one’s home\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نزح} \ar{كثير} \ar{من} \ar{الناس} \ar{بعد} \ar{الفيضان}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nazaḥa kathīr min an-nās baʿda al-fayaḍān.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Many people left their homes after the flood.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينزح}, \emph{yanzaḥ}.

A displaced person is \ar{نازح}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نزح}} (\emph{nazaḥa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-z-ḥ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to become far away\textquotedblright{}, and \textquotedblleft{}to draw all the water from a well\textquotedblright{}. People who must go far from home are \emph{nāziḥūn}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nazaḥa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nazaḥa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nazaḥa kathīr min an-nās baʿda al-fayaḍān.} — Many people left their homes after the flood.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to settle down, then the Arabic for to move out, then say \emph{nazaḥa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نزح} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To be displaced, to flee one’s home\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ودع} (waddaʿa)}{ودع (waddaʿa)}]{\ar{ودع} (waddaʿa) — to bid farewell}

\label{lesson:AR-C332-waddaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to move out, then the Arabic for to be displaced.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ودع}}
\textbf{\ar{ودع}} — \emph{waddaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to bid farewell\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ودعت} \ar{الأم} \ar{ابنها} \ar{في} \ar{المطار}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{waddaʿat al-umm ibnahā fī al-maṭār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mother said goodbye to her son at the airport.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يودع}, \emph{yuwaddiʿ}.

A farewell is \ar{وداع}; \ar{مع} \ar{السلامة} is what is said.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ودع}} (\emph{waddaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-d-ʿ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to leave, to let be\textquotedblright{}. It is Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to take leave of\textquotedblright{}; \emph{wadāʿ} is a farewell.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waddaʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waddaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waddaʿat al-umm ibnahā fī al-maṭār.} — The mother said goodbye to her son at the airport.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to move out, then the Arabic for to be displaced, then say \emph{waddaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ودع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To bid farewell\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 325–332 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R332-review-325-332}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for to witness and to swear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to witness, to swear, to take an oath, to confess, to deny
  \item a weapon, a sword, a spear, an arrow, armour
  \item that night, at the same time, as soon as, until, throughout
  \item to hold an event, to perform at, a procession, a banquet, an invited guest
  \item a revolution, to revolt, to become independent, independence, a country’s people
  \item to imprison, a prisoner, a prison cell, a shackle, to release
  \item to erect, to control, to extend, to flourish, an emperor
  \item to emigrate, to settle down, to move out, to be displaced, to bid farewell
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To witness? (\textbf{\ar{شهد}}, \emph{shahida}.) To swear? (\textbf{\ar{أقسم}}, \emph{aqsama}.) To take an oath? (\textbf{\ar{حلف}}, \emph{ḥalafa}.) To confess? (\textbf{\ar{اعترف}}, \emph{iʿtarafa}.) To deny? (\textbf{\ar{أنكر}}, \emph{ankara}.) A weapon? (\textbf{\ar{سلاح}}, \emph{silāḥ}.) A sword? (\textbf{\ar{سيف}}, \emph{sayf}.) A spear? (\textbf{\ar{رمح}}, \emph{rumḥ}.) An arrow? (\textbf{\ar{سهم}}, \emph{sahm}.) Armour? (\textbf{\ar{درع}}, \emph{dirʿ}.) That night? (\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{الليلة}}, \emph{fī tilka al-layla}.) At the same time? (\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{الوقت} \ar{نفسه}}, \emph{fī al-waqt nafsih}.) As soon as? (\textbf{\ar{حالما}}, \emph{ḥālamā}.) Until? (\textbf{\ar{إلى} \ar{أن}}, \emph{ilā an}.) Throughout? (\textbf{\ar{طوال}}, \emph{ṭuwāla}.) To hold an event? (\textbf{\ar{أقام}}, \emph{aqāma}.) To perform at? (\textbf{\ar{أحيا}}, \emph{aḥyā}.) A procession? (\textbf{\ar{موكب}}, \emph{mawkib}.) A banquet? (\textbf{\ar{وليمة}}, \emph{walīma}.) An invited guest? (\textbf{\ar{مدعو}}, \emph{madʿuww}.) A revolution? (\textbf{\ar{ثورة}}, \emph{thawra}.) To revolt? (\textbf{\ar{ثار}}, \emph{thāra}.) To become independent? (\textbf{\ar{استقل}}, \emph{istaqalla}.) Independence? (\textbf{\ar{استقلال}}, \emph{istiqlāl}.) A country’s people? (\textbf{\ar{شعب}}, \emph{shaʿb}.) To imprison? (\textbf{\ar{سجن}}, \emph{sajana}.) A prisoner? (\textbf{\ar{سجين}}, \emph{sajīn}.) A prison cell? (\textbf{\ar{زنزانة}}, \emph{zinzāna}.) A shackle? (\textbf{\ar{قيد}}, \emph{qayd}.) To release? (\textbf{\ar{أفرج}}, \emph{afraja}.) To erect? (\textbf{\ar{شيد}}, \emph{shayyada}.) To control? (\textbf{\ar{سيطر}}, \emph{sayṭara}.) To extend? (\textbf{\ar{امتد}}, \emph{imtadda}.) To flourish? (\textbf{\ar{ازدهر}}, \emph{izdahara}.) An emperor? (\textbf{\ar{إمبراطور}}, \emph{imbarāṭūr}.) To emigrate? (\textbf{\ar{هاجر}}, \emph{hājara}.) To settle down? (\textbf{\ar{استقر}}, \emph{istaqarra}.) To move out? (\textbf{\ar{رحل}}, \emph{raḥala}.) To be displaced? (\textbf{\ar{نزح}}, \emph{nazaḥa}.) To bid farewell? (\textbf{\ar{ودع}}, \emph{waddaʿa}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
